351471.title: The Alladi-like supernormal identity conjecture
351471.literal_statement:
Let $f(n)$ be an arithmetic function, let $\operatorname{idx}(p_n)=n$, let $p_{\operatorname{min}}(n)$ be the prime associated with the least prime factor of $n$, and define $\mu^*(n)=-\mu(n)$. Assume that

$$
\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{k=1}^{N}f(k)=L_f
$$

exists. **Alladi-like supernormal identity conjecture.** Then

$$
\sum_{n\geq 2}\frac{\mu^*(n)\left(f\circ\operatorname{idx}\right)\left(p_{\operatorname{min}}(n)\right)}{n}=L_f.
$$

The identity is proposed by transferring a partition-theoretic Abelian formula to natural numbers through the paper’s partition–prime analogies. No proof or resolution of this conjectural identity is given.
351471.precise_derivation_or_unpaid_gap: Cesaro convergence for arbitrary arithmetic f does not itself justify interchange with the least-prime-factor Mobius series or ordinary convergence. A uniform weighted Tauberian estimate or an explicit Cesaro-convergent divergent-series construction is missing. Finitely supported f would test only a degenerate subcase.

345884.title: Kuperberg's sharpness conjecture for triangulation enumeration
345884.literal_statement:
Let $a_0=1$, and for each positive integer $n$, let $a_n$ be the number of triangulations of a regular $n$-gon such that every internal vertex has degree at least $6$. Define the generating function

$$
A(x)=1+
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}a_nx^n.
$$

Let $b_n$ be the dimension of the invariant subspace in the $n$-th tensor power of the $7$-dimensional fundamental representation of $G_2$, and define

$$
B(x)=1+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}b_nx^n.
$$

Kuperberg's conjecture. The exponential growth rate of the triangulation numbers is

$$
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sqrt[n]{a_n}=\frac{7}{B(1/7)}.
$$

Equivalently, the radius of convergence of $A(x)$ is exactly $B(1/7)/7$. Kuperberg's identity $B(x)=A(xB(x))$ gives the corresponding upper bound on the growth rate, and the conjecture asserts that this bound is sharp.
345884.precise_derivation_or_unpaid_gap: Live search identifies exact public Scherer sharpness proof (2020 preprint/2024 publication and 2021 FPSAC theorem). Those actual guarded bodies were not acquired before network STOP. Do not call this new or authenticate its proof from excerpts.

375877.title: The Feedback-Exponent Conjecture for bounded minimum feedback vertex number
375877.literal_statement:
Let $k_0\geq 1$ be an integer. For a graph $H$, write $\operatorname{ex}(n,H)$ for its Turán number, and call a rational number $r\in[1,2]$ **realizable** as a Turán exponent if there is a graph $H$ such that

$$
\operatorname{ex}(n,H)=\Theta(n^r).
$$

The minimum feedback vertex number (FVN) of a graph is the minimum number of vertices whose removal makes the graph acyclic. **Feedback-Exponent Conjecture.** There exists a rational number $p/q\in[1,2]$ that cannot be realized as the Turán exponent of any bipartite graph whose minimum FVN is at most $k_0$.

This conjecture asks whether bounded minimum feedback vertex number restricts the rational exponents realizable by bipartite graphs. It is motivated by the Rational Exponent Conjecture of Erdős and Simonovits and by examples showing that, for bipartite graphs with minimum FVN $2$, the Turán exponent is not determined solely by the minimum cycle length; the status of the proposed restriction is not established in the supplied text.
375877.precise_derivation_or_unpaid_gap: For each k0 need a rational exponent excluded by EVERY bipartite graph of feedback vertex number<=k0. Such graphs have unbounded order; a finite type/countability shortcut cannot distinguish countably many exponents. Missing an all-size exponent restriction theorem.

375966.title: Zhu et al.'s generalized Turán conjecture for cycles with bounded circumference
375966.literal_statement:
For a graph $G$, let $N(C_q,G)$ denote the number of copies of the cycle $C_q$ in $G$, and let $\operatorname{ex}(n,C_q,\mathcal C_{\ge L+1})$ be the maximum possible value of $N(C_q,G)$ over all $n$-vertex graphs $G$ containing no cycle of length at least $L+1$. Let $H(n,L)$ be the Kopylov-type extremal graph on $n$ vertices with circumference at most $L$. **Zhu et al.'s conjecture.** For fixed integers $q\ge4$ and $L>q$, and all sufficiently large $n$, 

$$
\operatorname{ex}\bigl(n,C_q,\mathcal C_{\ge L+1}\bigr) =N\bigl(C_q,H(n,L)\bigr).
$$

This conjecture proposes that the Kopylov-type construction is asymptotically the exact extremal graph for counting copies of $C_q$ under a bounded-circumference restriction. The source indicates that the result is known for $q=4$ and $q=5$, while the stated general case remains open.

376018.title: Extremal-family conjecture for non-star intersecting s-stable families
376018.literal_statement:
Let $k\geq 4$, let $\binom{[n]}{k}_{s\text{-stable}}$ be the family of $s$-stable $k$-subsets of $[n]$, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family in this set. An intersecting family is one whose members pairwise intersect; it is a **non-star** family if it is not contained in a family of all sets containing a fixed element. Let $\tau(\mathcal{F})$ denote its covering number. For $x\in[n]$ and $Y\in\binom{[n]}{k}_{s\text{-stable}}$ with $x\notin Y$, define

$$
\mathcal{F}_{s,k}(x,Y)=\{Y\}\cup\{F\in\binom{[n]}{k}_{s\text{-stable}}\mid x\in F,\ F\cap Y\neq\emptyset\},
$$

and let $\mathcal{G}_{s,k}$ be the collection of all such families.

**Extremal-family conjecture.** If $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\binom{[n]}{k}_{s\text{-stable}}$ is a non-star intersecting family with $\tau(\mathcal{F})\geq 2$, then, for $n$ large enough—suggested in the source as $n\geq k(2s-1)+1$—

$$
|\mathcal{F}|\leq\max\{|F|\mid F\in\mathcal{G}_{s,k}\}.
$$

This is an extremal set-theoretic conjecture intended to identify the largest non-star intersecting families of $s$-stable sets. The source gives only a suggested threshold and does not provide a resolution.
376018.precise_derivation_or_unpaid_gap: Need stable-set spacing and source threshold conventions, followed by a compression/cross-intersection argument preserving s-stability and non-star status. Finite threshold obstructions cannot refute an unspecified sufficiently-large-n claim. Reference solved label is not a proof.

367192.title: Rücker, Rücker and Gutman's minimum principal-eigenvector concentration conjecture
367192.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple connected graph with vertex set $V(G)$, adjacency matrix $A_G$, and principal eigenvector $\underline{x}=(x_v)_{v\in V(G)}$ corresponding to the largest eigenvalue, with $x_v>0$. Define

$$
\Gamma_G:=\frac{\|\underline{x}\|_1^2}{\|\underline{x}\|_2^2}=\frac{\left(\sum_{v\in V(G)}x_v\right)^2}{\sum_{v\in V(G)}x_v^2}.
$$

Here $P_k$ denotes the path graph with $k$ vertices, and $K_4+P_{n-4}$ is obtained by attaching an endpoint of $P_{n-4}$ to the unique largest-degree vertex of $K_4$. **Rücker, Rücker and Gutman's conjecture.** If $n\geq 6$, then among $n$-vertex connected graphs, $\Gamma_G$ is minimized by

$$
G=K_4+P_{n-4}.
$$

The quantity $\Gamma_G$ measures how concentrated the principal eigenvector is; it satisfies $\Gamma_G\leq |V(G)|$, with equality precisely for regular graphs. The conjecture was presented as an extremal problem for connected graphs and is also related to questions about principal ratios and other measures of graph irregularity. The supplied source gives no evidence of resolution, so its status remains open.
367192.precise_derivation_or_unpaid_gap: Literal says attach to the unique largest-degree vertex of K4, although K4 is regular; the actual construction must be read, not silently repaired. No full all-connected-graph concentration comparison, finite witness or source proof established; wording correction earns zero.

371594.title: The conjecture characterizing graphs with fixed PSD propagation time one
371594.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph. A **PSD fast join** is a graph of order $n\geq 2$ such that $G\cong K_n$ or

$$
G\cong (K_{n_1}\mathbin{\,\dot{\cup}\,} K_{m_1})\vee \ldots \vee (K_{n_t}\mathbin{\,\dot{\cup}\,} K_{m_t}),
$$

for $t\geq 2$ and positive integers $n_i,m_i$ with $n=\sum_{i=1}^t n_i+m_i$. Here $\overline{\operatorname{pt}_+}(G)$ denotes the maximum positive semidefinite propagation time over minimum positive semidefinite forcing sets. **PSD fixed-propagation-time conjecture.** If $G$ is a connected graph and

$$
\overline{\operatorname{pt}_+}(G)=1,
$$

then $G$ is a PSD fast join. The theorem establishing the converse shows that PSD fast joins have fixed PSD propagation time equal to one; the conjecture is proved for graphs that are joins or have sufficiently large forcing numbers, while the general case remains open.

371817.title: Hypergraph Nash-Williams conjecture for clique decompositions
371817.literal_statement:
Let $q>r\geq 3$ be integers. An $r$-graph is an $r$-uniform hypergraph, and it is **$K_q^r$-divisible** when it satisfies the divisibility conditions necessary for a decomposition into copies of the complete $r$-graph $K_q^r$. Write $\delta(G)$ for the minimum $(r-1)$-degree and $v(G)$ for the number of vertices. **Hypergraph Nash-Williams conjecture.** If $G$ is a sufficiently large $K_q^r$-divisible $r$-graph such that

$$
\delta(G)\geq\left(1-\Theta_r\left(\frac{1}{q^{r-1}}\right)\right)\cdot v(G),
$$

then $G$ admits a $K_q^r$-decomposition. This conjecture generalizes Nash-Williams' triangle-decomposition conjecture to uniform hypergraphs. The source states that the paper proves a bound of order $1-c/q^{r-1+o(1)}$, approximately confirming the conjectured dependence on $q$, but does not establish the conjecture in its full stated form.

363832.title: The directed-clique conjecture for the minimum degree of digraphs
363832.literal_statement:
Let $D$ be a digraph, and let $\Delta_{\min}(D)$ denote its minimum degree parameter as defined in the paper. Let $\vec\chi(D)$ be its dichromatic number. A **directed clique** is a vertex set $X$ that can be partitioned into $(X_1,X_2)$ such that both $D[X_1]$ and $D[X_2]$ are complete digraphs and every possible arc from $X_1$ to $X_2$ is present. Let $\vec\omega(D)$ be the maximum size of a directed clique in $D$.

**Directed-clique conjecture.** There exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that every digraph $D$ satisfies

$$
\vec\chi(D)\leq\left\lceil(1-\varepsilon)\Delta_{\min}(D)+\varepsilon\vec\omega(D)\right\rceil.
$$

The conjecture is proposed after a related bound using the biclique number is shown to fail for $\Delta_{\min}$. It is presented as an open strengthening of the paper's partial result with $\widetilde{\Delta}$; no resolution is given.
363832.precise_derivation_or_unpaid_gap: Need actual Delta_min definition (do not conflate maximum of min local degrees with global minimum) and one epsilon working for every digraph. 364589.title: Mirzaei--Suk strengthening of Solymosi's forbidden configuration conjecture
364589.literal_statement:
Let $P$ be a set of $m$ points and let $\mathcal{L}$ be a set of $n$ lines in the plane. Write $I(P,\mathcal{L})$ for the set of incidences between points of $P$ and lines of $\mathcal{L}$, and let $G(P,\mathcal{L})$ be their incidence graph. Two configurations $(P_1,\mathcal{L}_1)$ and $(P_2,\mathcal{L}_2)$ are **isomorphic** when their incidence graphs are isomorphic.

**Mirzaei--Suk strengthening.** For any set of points $P_0$ and any set of lines $\mathcal{L}_0$ in the plane, there is a constant $\varepsilon=\varepsilon(P_0,\mathcal{L}_0)>0$ such that the maximum number of incidences between $n$ points and $n$ lines in the plane containing no subconfiguration isomorphic to $(P_0,\mathcal{L}_0)$ is $O(n^{4/3-\varepsilon})$.

This strengthens Solymosi's conjectured little-oh improvement of the Szemerédi--Trotter bound by requiring a fixed power saving depending on the forbidden configuration. The source presents it as open, although related special cases are known.
364589.precise_derivation_or_unpaid_gap: Need a power saving for every fixed realizable planar configuration, with precise subconfiguration conventions. A little-oh incidence bound or a special forbidden pattern cannot pay uniform positive epsilon for each arbitrary target. No such mechanism established.

365513.title: Alishahi–Taherkhani's extremal structure conjecture for almost intersecting families
365513.literal_statement:
Let $n$, $k$, and $s$ be positive integers with $k\geq 2$, and let $\mathcal{F}\subseteq \binom{[n]}{k}$ be an $s$-almost $1$-intersecting family such that

$$
\bigcap_{F\in\mathcal{F}}F=\emptyset.
$$

Assume that $n$ is sufficiently large. **Alishahi–Taherkhani's conjecture.** If $\mathcal{F}$ has maximum size, then

$$
\mathcal{F}\cong\left\\{F\in\binom{[n]}{k}:1\in F,\\ \left|F\cap[k+1]\right|\geq 2\right\\}\cup\mathcal{A}\cup\left\\{[k+1]\setminus\left\\{1\right\\}\right\\},
$$

where $\mathcal{A}$ is an $s$-subset of

$$
\left\\{F\in\binom{[n]}{k}:F\cap[k+1]=\left\\{1\right\\}\right\\}.
$$

This conjectures the extremal structure of maximum-sized almost intersecting families with empty total intersection, extending the asymptotically optimal upper bound established by Alishahi and Taherkhani for $t=1$.

365567.title: Product of Tribes optimality conjecture for small-shadow partitions
365567.literal_statement:
Let $b\in(0,1)$ and let $c=2^{bn}$. For a cover of $\mathcal{O}\mathcal{I}^n$ of size $c$, write $\rho_{n,n-1,c}$ for the relevant minimum maximum $(n-1)$-coordinate projection volume, and for a part $K$ and a coordinate set $A\subset[n]$ write $K_A$ for its projection onto $A$.

**Product of Tribes optimality conjecture.** There exists a universal constant $\delta$ such that

$$
\rho_{n,n-1,c}\geq\frac{1}{c}\left(1+\delta b\log(1/b)\right).
$$

Equivalently, for any cover of $\mathcal{O}\mathcal{I}^n$ of size $2^{bn}$, some part $K$ and some coordinate set $A\subset[n]$ with $|A|=n-1$ satisfy

$$
|K_A|\geq\frac{1}{c}\left(1+\delta b\log(1/b)\right).
$$

This formalizes the claim that the Product of Tribes construction cannot be substantially improved. The construction gives an upper bound of $\frac{1}{c}(1+O(b\log(1/b)))$, while the general lower bound is only $\frac{1}{c}(1+\Omega(b))$; the conjectured logarithmic factor remains unproved.

365679.title: Sparse Sperner conjecture for three central layers
365679.literal_statement:
Let $B_n$ be the Boolean lattice on $[n]$, let $N$ denote the size of a largest layer of $B_n$, and call the layers closest to the middle the **central layers**. For a function $\beta=\beta(n)$, consider antichains of size $\beta N$ in $B_n$.

**Sparse Sperner conjecture.** There exists a function $\beta^*(n)=\tilde\Theta(1/n)$ such that if $\beta\geq\beta^*(n)$, then almost all antichains of size $\beta N$ in $B_n$ are contained in three central layers.

This strengthens the proved result that the same conclusion holds for $\beta>C\log^2 n/\sqrt n$ for an absolute constant $C$. The conjectured threshold is motivated by the expected appearance of vertices two layers outside the middle, and the claim would follow from a suitable extension of the relevant container result to $\lambda=\tilde\Omega(1/n)$.

365976.title: The spectral extremal conjecture for 3-chromatic graph families
365976.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal F$ be a finite graph family, let $\chi(F)$ denote the chromatic number of a graph $F$, let $\mathrm{ex}(n,\mathcal F)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $\mathcal F$-free graph on $n$ vertices, let $T_{n,2}$ be the Turán graph with two parts, and let $\mathrm{SPEX}(n,\mathcal F)$ and $\mathrm{EX}(n,\mathcal F)$ denote, respectively, the spectrally extremal and extremal $\mathcal F$-free graphs. For sufficiently large $n$, suppose that

$$
\chi(F)=3,\qquad \mathrm{ex}(n,\mathcal F)\le e(T_{n,2})+Qn,
$$

where $Q<\frac{1}{3}$. **The spectral extremal conjecture.** For $n$ large enough,

$$
\mathrm{SPEX}(n,\mathcal F)\subseteq\mathrm{EX}(n,\mathcal F).
$$

This is the proposed weaker analogue, for $r=2$, of the paper's spectral extremal result for non-bipartite graph families with $r\geq 3$. The preceding proposition shows that the conclusion fails at the boundary value $Q=\frac{1}{3}$ for an infinite sequence of $n$; the conjectured range below that threshold remains open.

353195.title: Baruah–Begum conjecture on congruences for the smallest parts function of restricted overpartitions
353195.literal_statement:

$$
\overline{\operatorname{spt}}_\omega\left(5^{2k+\ell-1}(10n+5)\right)\equiv \overline{\operatorname{spt}}_\omega\left(5^{\ell-1}(10n+5)\right)\pmod{5^\ell},

\overline{\operatorname{spt}}_\omega\left(5^{2\ell}(10n+3)\right)\equiv\overline{\operatorname{spt}}_\omega\left(5^{2\ell}(10n+7)\right)\equiv0\pmod{5^{2\ell}}.

Let $f(n_1,\ldots,n_r,k,t)$ be the function specified in the cited formulation. Assume that $n_r$ is sufficiently large. **Han–Zhao's conjecture.**

\operatorname{ex}(n_1,\ldots,n_r,kK_t)=f(n_1,\ldots,n_r,k,t).

355981.title: Frankl's odd-parity extremal conjecture for t-intersecting k-Sperner families
355981.literal_statement:
Let $n,t,k$ be positive integers, and let ${\mathcal B}(t,k)$ denote the family constructed in the source: it contains the $(n+t-1)/2$-subsets containing $[1,t]$, all sets whose sizes range from $(n+t-1)/2+1$ through $(n+t-1)/2+k-1$, and the $(n+t-1)/2+k$-subsets not containing $[1,t]$. $$
|{\mathcal F}|\leq|{\mathcal B}(t,k)|=\binom{n-t}{\frac{n-t-1}{2}}+\sum_{i=1}^{k}\binom{n}{\frac{n+t-1}{2}+i}-\binom{n-t}{\frac{n-t-1}{2}+k}.
$$

The conjecture identifies ${\mathcal B}(t,k)$ as the largest such family for sufficiently large $n$; the source notes that a different candidate can be optimal for some small parameters.

350767.title: Second-, third- and fourth-minimum conjecture for the $A_\alpha$ spectral radius of strongly connected digraphs
350767.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a strongly connected digraph of order $n\geq 5$, and let $A_\alpha$ denote its $A_\alpha$ matrix and $\lambda_\alpha(G)$ its $A_\alpha$ spectral radius. For $0\leq \alpha<1$, let $\theta(0,1,n-3)$, $\theta(1,1,n-4)$ and $\theta(0,2,n-4)$ be the digraphs defined in the paper.

**Second-, third- and fourth-minimum conjecture.** Among all the strongly connected digraphs with order $n\geq 5$ and $0\leq \alpha<1$, $\theta(0,1,n-3)$, $\theta(1,1,n-4)$ and $\theta(0,2,n-4)$ are the digraphs which achieve the second, the third and the fourth minimum $A_\alpha$ spectral radius, respectively.

The result extends the preceding theorem, which establishes the same ordering for $0\leq \alpha\leq \frac{1}{2}$. The conjecture is proposed on the basis of numerical examples for the general range $0\leq \alpha<1$; no resolution is given in the supplied text.

351060.title: Cioabă–Gregory's maximum principal ratio conjecture for connected graphs
351060.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a simple, undirected connected graph on $n$ vertices. Let ${\bf x}$ be the positive unit eigenvector of its adjacency matrix corresponding to the largest eigenvalue, and define the **principal ratio** by

$$
\gamma(G):=\frac{x_{\max}}{x_{\min}},
$$

where $x_{\min}$ and $x_{\max}$ are the smallest and largest entries of ${\bf x}$. For integers $r,s\geq 1$, let $P_r\cdot K_s$ be the graph of order $r+s-1$ obtained by identifying an end vertex of the path $P_r$ with a vertex of the complete graph $K_s$; this is called a **kite graph**. **Cioabă–Gregory's conjecture.** Among all connected graphs on $n$ vertices, the kite graph attains the maximum principal ratio.

The conjecture identifies the extremal graph for the irregularity measure given by the principal ratio, extending the study of eigenvector bounds for connected graphs. The supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.

368393.title: Linear-diameter conjectures for list-recolouring graphs
368393.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a connected graph with $n$ vertices, and let $L$ be a list-assignment of $G$. Write $\mathcal{C}(G,L)$ for the $L$-recolouring graph and $\widehat{\mathcal{C}}(G,L)$ for the corresponding relaxed recolouring graph. **Linear-diameter conjectures.** (a) If, in addition to the conditions in the Key Lemma, $G$ has minimum degree at least $3$, then $\mathcal{C}(G,L)$ is connected and has diameter $O(n)$. (c) If, in addition to the conditions in the Main Theorem, $G$ has no path of degree-$2$ vertices of length more than $t$ for some $t\geq0$, then $\widehat{\mathcal{C}}(G,L)$ is connected and has diameter $O((t+1)n)$. These conjectures seek linear, or controlled near-linear, diameter bounds beyond the quadratic diameter forced by long induced paths of degree-$2$ vertices.
